title: MemCode: Discrete Semantic Representations for Long-Term Agent Memory
claim: Prior systems store raw context-dependent fragments and retrieve by surface similarity; ours writes atomic units and retrieves via dual complementary paths.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, red traditional vs blue proposed
description: Two horizontal bands compare memory pipelines. The top band, titled 'Traditional Approaches' with red labels, shows raw dialogue bubbles flowing through 'Write → Store → Retrieve'. Context-dependent fragments ('He said he'd come back yesterday', 'Tomorrow she will…') are scooped into a net by a worried robot, then dumped into a blue database. The final panel, 'Unstructured Memory', is a scatter of points where retrieval by surface similarity misses logically related but distant items, marked with a red X. The bottom band, 'Our Proposed Framework' with blue labels, shows the same dialogue input passing through a funnel that yields atomic facts (coreference resolved, time anchored). The flow then splits into Path A (vector embedding model → Vector DB) and Path B (VQ-VAE codebook → Codebook DB). Both paths merge into a green 'Dual-Path Structured & Connected Memory' panel with a connected cube graph, a checkmark, and 'Accurate, Aggregated Result'. The eye goes first to the red-versus-blue contrast between the two bands.
caption: Traditional memory pipelines store raw dialogue fragments and retrieve them primarily by surface similarity. Ours rewrites dialogue into atomic memory units and retrieves them through complementary vector and codebook paths.
abstract: Long-term memory remains a fundamental bottleneck for large language model (LLM) agents across sessions. Existing systems typically adopt a write-then-retrieve paradigm, storing context-dependent dialogue fragments and retrieving them via nearest-neighbor search in a continuous embedding space. This design yields unstable access units and systematically misses logically related but lexically distant evidence. We propose MemCode, a long-term agent memory framework that couples retrieval-oriented writing with discrete associative retrieval. MemCode rewrites dialogue into self-contained atomic memory units (AMUs), maps AMUs into a learnable codebook with isomorphic semantic quantization (ISQ), and uses codebook co-occurrence topology as a retrieval path complementary to vector search. For long-term memory stores, MemCode separates online atomic writes from asynchronous offline consolidation. On LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 backbones, MemCode achieves the best overall accuracy while keeping per-dialogue memory construction within roughly 40~130 seconds, making it 3~21 times faster than LightMem and over an order of magnitude faster than A-MEM and MemoryOS.
